title: preemptive-token-spill-and-cooperative-kernel-handoff-to-reduce-streaming-tail-latency
author: Claire Huang
description:
Motivation: We observed a persistent tail in streaming first-byte latency caused by frequent kernel preemption for very small microbatches and sporadic KV-cache misses that trigger synchronous warms. This PR introduces two complementary runtime techniques: 1) a predictive token-spill buffer that accepts very small emissions and defers kernel handoff until a short prediction window elapses (reduces preemption churn), and 2) a cooperative kernel-handoff mechanism that groups compatible streams into a short-lived cooperative run on the GPU to amortize kernel launch and context-switch cost. The result is lower p95/p99 TTFB across mixed short/long requests without increasing p50.

What changed (high level): added a predictive spill buffer and eviction heuristic, a cooperative handoff scheduler that matches by model variant and seqlen-range, speculative KV-cache rewarm hooks for in-flight spills, and a new live canary test and metrics to validate behavioral regressions. The description below contains a brief walk-through of the commits, changed areas, testing, and review notes. All narrative is continuous in this field.

- 0001Introduce predictive spill buffer and basic eviction policy
- 0002Implement cooperative kernel handoff coordinator and APIs
- 0003Add speculative KV rewarm hooks tied to spilled streams
- 0004Telemetry: metrics + tags for spill path and handoff latency
- 0005Integration tests and a small streaming canary; docs and examples
- 0006Fix race in handoff state machine after reviewer feedback
- 0007Tighten early-commit threshold and add feature flag (off by default)
review_conversation:
Ethan Cole: Observed a race when a spill is accepted and the handoff worker preempts it; can you add a state transition guard?
Claire Huang: Added a CAS-based guard in 0006, and added unit test coverage to exercise the transition.
Samir Patel: The heuristic thresholds seem tuned for our 8k-token workload; will this regress short-chat workloads?
Claire Huang: Added a guardrail: feature flag to enable handoff only for models with average response > 32 tokens and an opt-in annotation per route; default remains off for small-chat routes.
Rina Okafor: CI failed on the initial integration run (streaming_canary) due to flaky timing in the simulated KV warm; suggest a small backoff loop.
Claire Huang: Added a micro backoff and deterministic timing in canary harness; reran CI and green.
Ethan Cole: Approve after tests green and metrics look sane on canary.
Samir Patel: Small nit on metric names, but OK to merge once metrics doc updated.
Claire Huang: Addressed metric name nits and updated docs.
Merge-bot: Squash merged as commit 7a3d9c (squash).
ci_summary: Initial CI: failure on streaming_canary (timing-race) -> fixed by adding deterministic backoff and re-run. Full integration and unit test matrix passed. Binary smoke tests (linux-x86, cuda12) passed.
testing_and_benchmarks: Unit tests added for handoff state transitions and spill eviction; end-to-end streaming canary simulating mixed short/long workload. Canary results: p50 unchanged, p95 improved by ~18%, p99 improved by ~22% on a mixed 70/30 short/long traffic mix. Added microbench script for developers to reproduce: ci/integration/streaming_latency_check.sh
backwards_compatibility: Feature gated behind runtime flag 'predictive_spill_enabled' (default off). Route-level opt-in annotation 'streaming.handoff=enabled' introduced. No API breaking changes to public SDKs.
observability: New metrics: runtime.spill.count, runtime.spill.evictions, runtime.handoff.coop_latency_ms, runtime.handoff.batch_size, runtime.kv.rewarm.attempts. Docs updated at docs/observability/metrics_spill_handoff.md with guidance for alert thresholds.
deployment_notes: Feature is behind a cluster-level flag; recommend canary rollout to 5% of traffic in a non-critical region and monitor runtime.handoff.coop_latency_ms and runtime.spill.evictions for 48h before enabling globally. For Dedicated customers, coordinate with SRE for node-level kernel affinity settings.
release_notes: Streaming runtime: add predictive token spill buffer and cooperative kernel handoff to reduce streaming tail latency (opt-in, feature-flagged). Ship behind feature flag; p95/p99 improvements in mixed workloads. Metrics and canary included.
